request: Rewrite this proposal for the engineering manager who approves it.
input:
# Proposal: background job queue

It was decided that we need a proper job queue for background work. Image resize jobs run inside the web request today, and users see timeouts on uploads larger than 5 MB.

We looked at three options: pg-boss, BullMQ, and SQS. Both options have their merits, and the right choice depends on the needs of the team.

- pg-boss is scalable and reliable. In a staging test on 2026-10-10 it handled 350 jobs per second with 4 workers. It runs on our existing Postgres.
- BullMQ is battle-tested and flexible. It needs Redis. The managed plan costs about $90 a month, and the platform team would need to run it.
- SQS is enterprise-grade. Local development needs localstack or an AWS account for each developer, and our integration tests run offline in CI.

Our load is about 2 jobs per second, and up to 15 per second during the nightly import.

Risks: the jobs table may grow without limit. Mitigation: we will monitor closely and follow best practices. If Postgres is down, the queue is down.

The platform team leans toward pg-boss, because it adds no new system. A decision was made to look at this again if the load passes 200 jobs per second.

The platform team will review this proposal on 2026-11-20.
